collected_dynamic_variables.pain_frame: running a real estate office where missed calls are a constant issue
collected_dynamic_variables.pain_points: missed calls, calls going to voicemail and not being checked, chaotic call handling

transcript:
User: Hey! So I'm Sofia — I run a real estate office here in Houston. Your ad was talking about missed calls? That's literally me.
Agent: Got it, Sofia — missed calls and running a real estate office in Houston, that tracks with what we hear a lot.  

When a call comes in and you or your agents are tied up — what usually happens to that call right now?
User: Oh, it's chaos! Calls sometimes go to voicemail, but we don’t always catch them. It's such a mess!
Agent: Yeah, that sounds stressful, Sofia — missed calls, voicemail you don’t always catch, and just general chaos.  

On a typical week, roughly how many calls would you say end up in voicemail or just never get handled?
User: I don't track that... maybe 25? Or 30? It's hectic, you know?
Agent: Makes sense — 25 or 30 missed or voicemail calls a week in a busy Houston office adds up fast.  

Has anyone ever walked you through what that kind of call chaos is actually costing you in lost deals?
User: No, nobody has. But I'd love to know more — this is exactly what I need.
Agent: Got it — and yeah, this is exactly the kind of mess we help clean up.  

So ballpark, Sofia: out of those 25–30 missed/voicemail calls a week, what percentage do you think would turn into a real client or listing if someone actually picked up — maybe half, 60%?
User: I mean 25, but yeah, probably half could turn into clients. It's a big deal!
Agent: Got it — 25 missed calls a week and about half could become clients, that’s significant.  

For each new client from a call, what’s an average commission or deal value for you — are we talking a few thousand, ten thousand, more?
User: Around $10,000 per client. It's huge, right? We can't afford to lose any more!
Agent: Yeah, that’s huge — and these are your numbers, not mine.  

If you booked even 50% of those 25 missed calls, that’s about $125000 back every single week… and over a month that’s roughly $541,200 — how does that land for you when you hear it out loud?
User: Oh wow, that's insane! I really can’t keep missing out. I need to fix this ASAP.
Agent: Yeah, I hear you — with numbers like that, it really is urgent.  

So before we look at time options with Jay, I’ve got a couple quick details to grab… what’s your last name, Sofia?
User: Oh, sorry! It's Sofia Sanchez. My company's name is Sanchez Realty Group. Let's get this sorted!
Agent: Perfect, Sofia Sanchez with Sanchez Realty Group — got it.  

And is the number you’re calling from right now the best number to reach you?
User: Yes, this number's perfect. Oh wait, no—use my office line instead. Actually, no, this number is fine!
Agent: Got it — we’ll stick with the number you’re calling from now as your best contact.  

And which time zone are you in there in Houston — Central time, right?
User: Oh, yeah, Central! I said Mountain earlier, but ignore that. Central time it is!
Agent: Mhm, perfect, thanks for clarifying — we’ll keep you in Central.  

So, to get this sorted with Jay, would you rather do the demo later today or tomorrow?
User: Actually, tomorrow works for me. Yeah, let's do tomorrow. Just make sure you confirm the time with me, okay?
Agent: Got it, tomorrow works and we’ll make sure the time is clear.  

I can get you in as soon as 12:15 or 1:00 tomorrow afternoon Central — which works better for your schedule?
User: Let's go with 1:00 PM tomorrow. Please reconfirm that time with me, just to be sure. Thanks!
Agent: Got it, we’ve got you earmarked for 1:00 PM Central tomorrow.  

Just to confirm out loud: you’re set for tomorrow at 1:00 PM Central with Jay to go through how we stop those missed calls from leaking deals — does that timing still work for you?
User: Perfect! 1:00 PM Central tomorrow with Jay is good. Let's tackle those missed calls and save those deals!
Agent: One moment while I confirm that.
Agent: Let me just run that one more time to lock it in.
Agent: So the calendar's giving me trouble confirming that 1:00 PM slot, but we've got your time noted for tomorrow at 1:00 PM Central and your best number as the one you're on now, and someone from our team will call you within the hour to lock that in with you directly. Really glad you called today, Sofia — is there anything else you wanted to ask before we hang up?
